Growing up with limited formal education, I learned to appreciate its practical side through physics and philosophy. It’s challenging but satisfying when I connect it to real-world patterns.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I rarely feel anxious about math because I’ve built confidence through hands-on problem-solving. My focus on practical applications and curiosity helps me stay calm. Anxiety might pop up during complex proofs, but I break them into small steps.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used a math-solving app to check my work on algebra problems. It was helpful for verifying steps but not for deep understanding. I found it useful for quick validation but preferred manual practice for solidifying concepts.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug these x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. Check if they’re maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
